name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with t(6;9)(p23;q34)
aliases: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with DEK-NUP214 fusion

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of t(6;9)(p23;q34) translocation confirmed by cytogenetics or FISH
Bone marrow or peripheral blood blasts ≥20%
Myeloid lineage confirmed by flow cytometry with expression of CD13, CD33, and CD34
Detection of DEK-NUP214 fusion transcript by RT-PCR

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ≥20% myeloid blasts in bone marrow or blood combined with confirmed t(6;9)(p23;q34) translocation or DEK-NUP214 fusion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: This subtype is associated with poor prognosis and often shows multilineage dysplasia.

searchTerms: immature white blood cells in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow hypercellularity with myeloid blast proliferation
searchTerms: bone marrow crowded with immature myeloid cells
high myeloid blast count in marrow

common.symptomName: Anemia-related pallor and dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: pale skin and shortness of breath

common.symptomName: Thrombocytopenia leading to petechiae and mucosal bleeding
searchTerms: low platelets causing bruising and bleeding
easy bruising and mucous membrane bleeding
low neutrophil count with frequent infections
repeated bacterial infections due to low white cells

common.symptomName: Fever due to infection or leukemic process

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

searchTerms: losing weight and sweating at night

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement
lung problems from blood cell buildup

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing myeloblasts with Auer rods
Bone marrow biopsy hypercellular with >20% myeloblasts
Cytopenias including anemia, thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia
imaging: Chest X-ray may show infiltrates secondary to infection or leukostasis
Ultrasound or CT may reveal hepatosplenomegaly
other: Flow cytometry showing myeloid markers CD13, CD33, CD34 positivity

distinguishingFeatures: Better prognosis compared to t(6;9) AML

redFlags: Rapidly increasing peripheral blood blast count
Signs of leukostasis such as respiratory distress or neurological deficits
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
